title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Tech Catches the Evening Swell as SpaceX Soars
conditions.summary: Stocks rose for a fourth straight session as chipmakers and SpaceX led the Nasdaq up about 1%. Breadth was roughly even, and yields stayed near multi-decade highs.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: S&P 500 rose 0.6% to 7,757.71, the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.05% to 26,702.86, and the Dow added 0.7% to 52,856.09, a one-month high.
The Russell 2000 rose 0.3% to 2,781.02.
Tech and chip stocks led after SpaceX's strong first quarterly report as a public company renewed AI enthusiasm; Nvidia rose 2.5%.
Cybersecurity stocks rallied after a critical PHP software flaw was disclosed; energy stocks rose modestly.
Breadth was nearly flat: 1,361 NYSE advancers versus 1,347 decliners.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: The 10-year Treasury yield rose about 3 basis points to roughly 5.15%.
A 20-year Treasury auction sold at 5.469%, the highest yield for that auction since 1986.
WTI crude held near $97.60 while Brent sat near $110 after an attack on a Saudi oil field; the US ordered some embassy staff out of Saudi Arabia.
Gold was near $4,151, bitcoin rose about 2.3% to about $84,600, the dollar index slipped to 101.5 and the VIX fell to 16.68.
No major US economic data today; EIA crude stocks fell 3.06 million barrels versus a 0.82 million draw expected. The Fed is in its quiet period before its Oct 28 decision.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: SMCI (Super Micro Computer): +9.6% — raised its fiscal first-quarter revenue forecast to $18.5–19.5 billion.
SPCX (SpaceX): +7.8% — first profit as a public company, with AI nearly half of sales.
ZS (Zscaler): +7.9% — cybersecurity stocks jumped after a critical PHP flaw was disclosed.
COIN (Coinbase) and CRCL (Circle): +4% or more — a federal banking regulator finalized stablecoin rules.
IBM (IBM): +4.0% — led Dow gainers.
T (AT&T): -6.4% — added fewer postpaid phone customers than expected amid Starlink Mobile competition.
NFLX (Netflix): -5.3% — fourth-quarter revenue forecast missed and it cut its 2026 ad revenue outlook to $2.7 billion.
DXCM (DexCom): -6.4% — among the S&P 500's worst performers.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Danaher rose 4.3% after adjusted EPS of $2.11 topped the $1.92 estimate and it raised full-year guidance.
Thermo Fisher gained about 4% and Philip Morris about 5.6% in afternoon trading after third-quarter reports.

Meta beat after the close: adjusted EPS of $7.40 versus $5.74 expected and revenue of $64.6 billion versus $63.4 billion; it declared a one-time Class C share dividend, effectively a 2-for-1 split. Shares rose roughly 3% to 6% after hours.
Tesla beat after the close: adjusted EPS of $0.48 versus $0.43 and revenue of $28.05 billion versus $27.88 billion. Shares rose about 1% after hours.

sections.title: Business News
items: Elon Musk said SpaceX and Tesla have each formed special committees to discuss a potential merger.
Anthropic may publicly file its IPO registration as soon as Friday.
A federal banking regulator finalized stablecoin rules, lifting crypto-linked stocks.
Russia told US envoy Steve Witkoff it is ready to resume three-way talks with the US and Ukraine, possibly around Nov 10.
France's 10-year bond yield touched 5% for the first time since 2002.

sections.title: On Deck
items: 7:30 AM CT: weekly jobless claims (forecast 200,000); 9:00 AM CT: Leading Index for September (forecast -0.2%).
Before the open: Procter & Gamble, Lockheed Martin, Honeywell, Comcast, Union Pacific, Blackstone and American Airlines.
After the close: Newmont, Western Digital, Deckers, Boston Beer and VeriSign.
No Fed speakers: the Fed is in its quiet period before the Oct 28 decision.
SpaceX faces a lockup expiration of up to 1.3 billion shares.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Wednesday, October twenty-first, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is sliding into the water, and my board is waxed for tomorrow. Gus the wonder dog spent the afternoon chasing sandpipers. Give the crew a howdy, Gus! Let's start with the final set, and it was a good one. The S and P five hundred rose about six tenths of a percent to seven thousand seven hundred fifty-seven. The Nasdaq Composite led the way, up a little over one percent to twenty-six thousand seven hundred three. The Dow climbed seven tenths of a percent to fifty-two thousand eight hundred fifty-six. The Russell two thousand added about a quarter of a percent. Tech and chipmakers carried the swell. SpaceX lit up the lineup after its first profit as a public company, and the stock jumped almost eight percent. Hang Ten! Breadth was close to even, though, so this was a tech ride more than a wide one. Now the wind and weather. The ten year Treasury yield edged up about three basis points to around five point one five percent. Oil stayed choppy near ninety-seven dollars a barrel after an attack on a Saudi oil field. Gold was little changed near four thousand one hundred fifty dollars, bitcoin rose about two percent, and the V I X fear gauge slipped to about sixteen point seven. There were no big U S economic reports today, and the Fed is in its quiet period before next Wednesday's decision. Here's the lineup. Super Micro Computer surged about nine and a half percent after raising its revenue forecast. Gus, that wave is worth a biscuit! Here you go, buddy! Cybersecurity names like Zscaler jumped about eight percent after a serious software flaw came to light. On the wipeout side, A T and T fell about six percent, and Netflix dropped about five percent after a light revenue forecast. Gnarly. On the tide chart, Danaher rose about four percent after beating profit estimates and raising its outlook, and Thermo Fisher and Philip Morris both rallied after morning reports. After the bell, Meta beat on sales and profit, and the stock jumped in late trading. Tesla also beat on revenue and profit and edged higher after hours. Stoked! Over at beach talk, Elon Musk says SpaceX and Tesla have each formed special committees to discuss a possible merger. Anthropic could file publicly for its I P O as soon as Friday. Tomorrow's forecast. Weekly jobless claims land at seven thirty A M Central, and the leading index at nine A M Central. Before the open we hear from Procter and Gamble, Lockheed Martin and Honeywell. After the close, it's Newmont and Western Digital. No Fed speakers, since they're in the quiet room. Catch the Dawn Patrol tomorrow morning. Got a stock, an E T F or a futures contract on your mind? Type it into the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will call that wave for you. This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
